findings.reason: the report section must name `review/audits.py` as its lint source, or the builder will add a third lint beside the one the dependency plan builds (and `harmonize.lint_links`, `harmonize.py:499`, is already a duplicate of `run_link_integrity`).
findings.text: §2's report lists "the lint findings by class" but never names the producer; the conformance checks `sn-house-style` §4 builds land in `imas_codex/standard_names/docs_gates.py:660` (`house_style_findings`) and reach the pipeline through `imas_codex/standard_names/review/audits.py:99` (`AuditReport`), with `run_lexical_lint` (`review/audits.py:296`) and `run_link_integrity` (`review/audits.py:405`) as the other two classes. `sn-house-style` §4 states in its own text that "the harmonize command reads the same report", so the source is already decided and the plan should cite it rather than leave it unnamed.

findings.reason: extend `protection.py` with the roster/`contested` reasons and reuse its evidence string, or the command's guard and the owner's guard will disagree on what "recommended" means.
findings.text: §3's guard refuses three classes ("recommended into a catalog pull request": roster members of an open candidate request, `name_stage` `approved`, and `contested`) unless `--force` is given. `protection.py` already owns this concept: `automatic_deletion_protections` returns per-identity durable-authority evidence that bars a write, and its query already names `name_stage = 'approved'` (`protection.py:109`) and `catalog_pr_number IS NOT NULL` (`protection.py:111`). The plan forks a second query for the same "this name is committed, do not move it" question.

findings.reason: the apply section should call `mark_members_for_regen` directly on the pattern family's members, or state why re-keying the parent-level wrapper is needed; as written it is a thin layer that hides nothing.
findings.text: §3 says `sn harmonize --apply` "is the caller of `mark_families_for_regen` ... adapted to take a pattern family". `mark_families_for_regen` resolves members through `HAS_PARENT` (`harmonize.py:660-682`) — the very grouping §1 says is wrong — and delegates to `mark_members_for_regen(member_ids)` (`harmonize.py:542`), which already takes an explicit member set, snapshots each member's docs, resets the pipeline and stamps a scope `run_id`. A pattern family yields exactly that member set from `families.fetch_pattern_family` (`families.py:605`). No behaviour in the parent-level wrapper survives the re-key beyond a `HAS_PARENT` lookup the plan does not want.

findings.reason: with every budget figure at 0 the section must enumerate the dead helpers it orphans and account for the new refusal family in its own text, or name why neither can be retired.
findings.text: public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0. §2 adds a new top-level command with a scope group (`--batch`/`--family`/`--concept`/`--all`) and a mode group (`--report`/`--apply`/`--dry-run`/`--cost-limit`), and names only two retirements (`--families`, `--target groups`). Deleting `--target groups` (`sn.py:6193`) orphans its helpers, which the section does not name: `_refuse_grouped_review_scoping` (`sn.py:5952`), `_report_drifting_families` (`sn.py:5993`) and `harmonize.build_worklist` (`harmonize.py:298`), whose only production caller is `sn.py:6211`. §3 adds a refusal family and a `--force` with a recorded reason, and names no existing refusal it retires or merges.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the command hides scope resolution, pattern-family assembly (`families.py`), the drift metric, the lint read and the apply/snapshot behind one surface, delegating work to the existing deep modules rather than spreading a fan of wrappers over one mechanism.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3's refusal guard for "recommended into a catalog pull request" re-implements the durable-authority evidence query that `protection.py` already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §2 adds a new command and §3 a new refusal family and `--force`, naming only two flag retirements and not the now-orphaned helpers, and stating no reason the added surface cannot be retired or merged.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §1 does cite the three scattered surfaces (`harmonize.py`, `sn run --families`, `sn review --target groups`) and §3 cites `mark_families_for_regen` and `select_anchor`, but §2's report measures "the lint findings by class" without naming the module that already produces them (`house_style_findings`, `docs_gates.py:660`; the `AuditReport` in `review/audits.py`).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 proposes adapting `mark_families_for_regen` to take a pattern family without saying why `mark_members_for_regen`, which already snapshots, resets and stamps a scope run-id over an explicit member set, cannot be called directly.
